manifest.name: @royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo
manifest.description: dsh plugin + agent preset that replicates opencode + oh-my-openagent (omo): opencode's toolchain and system prompt, omo's multi-role subagent orchestration, and browser-side omo role selection + per-role model/fallback settings.

scripts.test: node scripts/check-architecture.mjs && node scripts/check-alignment.mjs && node --test tests/*.spec.mjs

bundle.text:
# Bundle patch for @royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo.
#
# The package's own host row owns the volatile `opencode-omo` settings entry
# (role/session maps) and the `ctx.omoRoles` service. The `opencode-omo`
# agent preset is declared with the official @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset row;
# its plugin list is generated from presets/opencode-omo/agent.cordis.yml.
#
# Run `node scripts/sync-preset-declaration.mjs` after editing the composition;
# tests/preset-declaration.spec.mjs fails when the embedded list drifts.
- insert:
    - id: opencode-omo
      name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo'
- insert:
    - id: preset-opencode-omo
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: opencode-omo
        name: "opencode-omo"
        description: "复刻 opencode + omo (oh-my-openagent) 行为模式：opencode 的工具链与完整系统提示，加上 omo 的多角色编排（sisyphus/plan builder/plan executor 等主角色 + oracle/librarian/explore/metis/momus/looker 专家）、输入框角色选择、按角色模型/fallback 配置与 AGENTS.md 上下文注入。"
        order: 5
        plugins:
          # The `opencode-omo` agent preset: opencode's toolchain and system prompt,
          # plus omo (oh-my-openagent)'s multi-role subagent orchestration.
          #
          # This is an AGENT-PLANE composition mounted once per process under a standing
          # scope; each session naming this preset joins by scope parentage. Host-plane
          # rows (registries, sandbox, persistence, model route) stay in the web bundle.

          # ── identity / loop shim ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # The `./driver.mjs` row registers opencode's complete system prompt
          # (persona.md + omo Sisyphus identity) as a DYNAMIC system-prompt section on
          # the native `systemPrompt` seam. Its text provider prepends opencode's live
          # <env> block and swaps in the selected omo role's prompt per assembly, and its
          # listeners apply opencode tool gating, maxSteps, ultrawork, and role model
          # fallback — no dsh-side driver seam required.
          - id: opencode-omo-loop
            name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/driver.mjs'

          # AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md walk-up injection, mirroring opencode's instruction loading.
          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536

          # ── rules injection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # omo's rules-injector text is folded into the complete system prompt by
          # driver.mjs (a systemPrompt.context row would be dropped together with the
          # suppressed runtime context).
          #
          # ── comment-checker hook ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # omo's comment-checker: reject AI-slop comments on write/edit before execution.
          - id: opencode-omo-comment-checker
            name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/comment-checker.mjs'

          # opencode external_directory + doom_loop permission rules (tools/pre-execute).
          - id: opencode-omo-permission-rules
            name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/permission-rules.mjs'

          # bash sandbox-escalation shim: the stock persistent bash carries none of
          # tool-bash's sandbox_permissions/approval contract, so under workspace-write
          # an out-of-workspace write dead-ends at EROFS. This per-agent shim adds the
          # contract back using only public dsh services (see the module header).
          - id: opencode-omo-escalating-bash
            name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/escalating-bash.mjs'

          # ── lsp ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # omo's LSP surface (named lsp_* tools over dsh's single `lsp` / ctx.lsp.query).
          # The optional module self-disables when the LSP packages or the TypeScript
          # server are absent, so an npm-only install still mounts this preset.
          - id: opencode-omo-lsp
            name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/lsp-optional.mjs'

          # ── shell ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # opencode's shell is persistent; dsh's fresh `tool-bash` is replaced with the
          # persistent PTY-backed bash so state survives across calls, matching opencode.
          - id: persistent-shell
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              terminals: true
            config:
              - id: pty
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-terminal'

              - id: terminal-bash
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-terminal-bash'
                config:
                  timeoutMs: 300000

              - id: persistent-bash
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash-persistent'
                config:
                  timeoutMs: 300000
                  description: |-
                    Run commands in a bash shell.
                    * State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user.
                    * To inspect a particular line range of a file, e.g. lines 10-25, try 'sed -n 10,25p /path/to/the/file'.
                    * Please avoid commands that may produce a very large amount of output.
                    * Please run long-lived commands in the background, e.g. 'sleep 10 &' or start a server in the background.
                    * Chain independent commands with ';' or '&&' to batch them in one call.

          - id: tool-pwsh
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
            disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'

          # ── filesystem ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # opencode's execution backend is the raw local filesystem. Give this mode its
          # own `ctx.fs` (local, full-access, session-cwd-resolved) in an isolate realm so
          # file tools use opencode's fs semantics and other modes keep the sandboxed host fs.
          - id: filesystem
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              fs: true
            config:
              - id: fs-local
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local'

              - id: tool-fs
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'

              - id: tool-fs-search
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
                config:
                  sampleOverCapGlobResults: false

              # apply_patch and hashline live in this realm so they use the same local fs
              # as read/write/edit (full access, matching opencode's execution backend).
              - id: opencode-omo-apply-patch
                name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/apply-patch.mjs'

              - id: opencode-omo-tool-surface
                name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/tool-surface.mjs'

              - id: opencode-omo-hashline
                name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/hashline.mjs'

          # ── background jobs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'

          # Model-visible OpenCode/omo names (background_output / background_cancel)
          # over the dsh jobs + subagent execution layer. Hides job_* / subagent from
          # the assembled catalog the same way tool-surface hides dsh web_search.queries.
          - id: opencode-omo-delegation-surface
            name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/delegation-surface.mjs'

          # dsh stand-in for omo's Codex Stop continuation: steer while Boulder work
          # for this session still has unchecked plan checkboxes.
          - id: opencode-omo-start-work-continuation
            name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/start-work-continuation.mjs'

          # ── skills ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # omo ships its skills beside the plugin. `omo-skills.mjs` registers them as
          # `user-dsh`-sourced skills (not `custom`), so the third-party
          # @maintainall/dsh-plugin-skills-manager recognises and can enable/disable
          # them through its existing global/workspace/session override store without
          # any change to that plugin. The native filesystem provider keeps its default
          # project/user roots.
          - id: omo-skills
            name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/omo-skills.mjs'

          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'

          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'

          # ── omo builtin commands ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # Native dsh command registrations for the omo slash-command surface.
          - id: opencode-omo-commands
            name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/omo-commands.mjs'

          # ── goals ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # omo's goal feature (create_goal / get_goal / update_goal) maps here.
          - id: tool-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'

          # ── plan mode ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # opencode's plan agent (plan_enter / plan_exit) maps here.
          - id: planning
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              planMode: true
            config:
              - id: plan-mode
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
                config:
                  section: |
                        You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until exit_plan_mode succeeds or the user switches the session mode. Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.

                        Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer existing functions and patterns over new machinery.

                        The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability. These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase: it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself belongs in exit_plan_mode.

                        Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you can find out.

                        Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.

                        When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.

          # ── compaction ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'

              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'

              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 8192
                  headChars: 4096
                  tailChars: 1024

          # ── delegation and workflows ────────────────────────────────────────────────
          # omo's multi-role subagents: each named tool carries its own tool
          # restrictions. The child system prompt is the driver's complete
          # `<env>` + specialist body (role pinned at spawn); a static persona
          # overlay would shadow that section and restore the dsh harness identity.
          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              workflowEngine: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent-control
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'

              - id: tool-subagent-list-agents
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents'

              - id: tool-subagent
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: subagent

              - id: tool-subagent-fork
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: fork
                  toolName: subagent_fork

              # Prometheus planner. `plan` must be a registered global toolName: every
              # named-row deny list includes it, and dsh `tools.restrict()` throws on
              # unknown names (so omitting this row breaks librarian/explore/oracle spawn).
              - id: role-plan
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: plan
              # omo's read-only specialist subagents.
              - id: role-oracle
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: oracle
              - id: role-librarian
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: librarian
              - id: role-explore
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: explore
              - id: role-metis
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: metis
              - id: role-momus
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: momus
              - id: role-looker
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: multimodal-looker
              # Council reviewers (composer athena / athena-junior / council-member).
              - id: role-athena
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: athena
              - id: role-athena-junior
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: athena-junior
              - id: role-council-member
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: council-member
              # omo's primary agents are also delegatable named subagents in the
              # reference roster. Delegated primary roles with DENY_PRIMARY use worker
              # prompts; recursion into subagent/workflow tools is denied so a worker
              # cannot silently spawn another orchestrator tree.
              - id: role-sisyphus
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: sisyphus
              - id: role-hephaestus
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: hephaestus
              - id: role-atlas
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: atlas
              - id: role-sisyphus-junior
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: sisyphus-junior
              - id: opencode-omo-task-shim
                name: '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/presets/opencode-omo/task-shim.mjs'

              - id: workflow-ptc
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
              - id: tool-workflow
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow'

              - id: tool-ralph
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ralph'
                config:
                  subagentProvider: spawn
                  maxRounds: 64

          # ── remaining model-facing rows ─────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'

          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true

          # opencode's websearch / webfetch.
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: true
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000

readme.text:
[](https://github.com/royenheart/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo/tree/dsh-migrate/state)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds an `opencode-omo` agent preset (mode) to the web profile. The mode replicates the behavior of **opencode** + the **omo** plugin ([oh-my-openagent](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent)), scoped to this mode only — other presets (`standard`/…) keep the default dsh loop, sandboxed fs, and no omo hooks.

- **opencode + omo system prompt** — the real opencode `default.txt` persona (tone, style, proactiveness, conventions, code style, task guidance) + omo's Sisyphus orchestrator identity, declared as the **complete** system prompt: the dsh harness identity and runtime-context snapshot are suppressed for this mode. The loop shim additionally prepends opencode's **live environment block** (exact model id, working dir, workspace root, git, platform, date, recomputed every step).
- **omo role picker in the composer** — in dsh's existing `conversation.input.left` tool-row slot (after the access/plan chips), the primary/all roles `sisyphus`, `hephaestus` (Deep Agent), `prometheus` (Plan Builder), `atlas` (Plan Executor), and `sisyphus-junior`. Selecting one swaps the session's complete system prompt and applies that role's configured model. Specialist roles (`athena`, `athena-junior`, `council-member`, `metis`, `momus`, `oracle`, `librarian`, `explore`, `multimodal-looker`) are reached through `task(subagent_type=...)`, not the composer picker.
- **Global "Role Settings"** in the dsh settings panel (`settings.section`): per-role primary model dropdown (follow current / omo default / fixed)

```
cordis.patch.yml                 # bundle patch: host row + official agent-preset declaration
patches/                         # dsh-side patch(es) still required for the complete surface
install.py                       # idempotent install/uninstall (manifest + missing runtime/LSP links)
src/                             # host + client plugin halves (role registry, settings, picker UI)

`lib/` is generated locally and is not committed. `install.py` always builds the repository's own toolchain first (`npm ci` when the toolchain is missing or `package-lock.json` is newer than the installed lock, then `npm run build`) and exits with an actionable error if npm, the build, the artifacts, or a required harness link is missing:

```sh
python3 install.py install --profile web              # install (idempotent)
python3 install.py uninstall --profile web            # remove
```

`install.py` symlinks the package into `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/`, mirrors runtime packages only when absent, ensures/repoints the LSP links (refusing real directories), and edits the profile's `package.json` (adds/removes the dependency + bundle entry). The bundle patch declares both the host row and the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row, so there is no separate user-preset-root copy.

Manual alternative — the package is a dsh **bundle**: it declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and ships the preset. `dsh plugin` reconciles `dsh.profile.bundles` from the installed package automatically:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-plugin-opencode-omo
```

The bundle patch declares the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row for `opencode-omo`, so no `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets` copy is published. Restart dsh and select **opencode-omo** from the mode picker.

**Upgrading from the pre-0.2.1 row id.** Existing profiles used the
`opencode-omo-roles` settings entry; rc.2's legacy importer preserves that
unknown entry in `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml.imported`. On boot the host row reads that backup once per profile and merges its
role/session maps into the active `opencode-omo` entry, so old role models and
fallbacks are not silently reset. Profiles migrated by the pre-release
`9ad557c` home-global marker may re-import once because that marker had no
profile identity; review the merged roles after upgrading.

**Optional LSP server.** The preset preconfigures `typescript-language-server` for the `lsp_*` navigation tools. `install.py` checks `PATH` and warns when it is missing; the optional LSP module then mounts without a provider so the mode still loads (LSP queries fail gracefully instead of blocking the whole preset). Install it to enable LSP:

```sh
npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript
```

then restart dsh.

**web_fetch provider.** The preset enables dsh's native `web_fetch` tool (`fetch: true`). Official 0.2.1 already registers `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-fetch-http` in the base bundle, so this plugin does **not** insert a second fetch row (that would throw `WEB_DUPLICATE_PROVIDER`). `web_search` keeps using the existing DeepSeek search provider (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`). Other presets keep `fetch: false`, so their tool surface is unchanged.

One patch is still required for the complete opencode surface:

`patches/0001-agent-pre-step-assistant-prefill.patch` (rebased onto
`dsh-v0.2.1-rc.2`) adds `PreStepDecision.assistantPrefill`, a request-only
assistant tail. The loop logs it on `request/header`, appends it to exactly the
request that asked for it, and prices it in token pressure; it is never a
session `assistant/message`, so transcript, compaction, and stats stay clean.

Apply it to the dsh checkout with the instructions in
[`patches/README.md`](patches/README.md); `install.py` does not modify the harness
checkout. Without the patch the preset still loads and uses the fallback below.

**Why the patch is still required.** opencode appends `MAX_STEPS_PROMPT` as an
assistant-role continuation on the ceiling step. Official 0.2.1
`PreStepDecision` is still `reject | { kind: 'enter', messages, startsRequestSeries? }`,
and `agent/request` cannot mutate request messages, so no official extension
point can express a request-only assistant tail. Upstream request:
[discussion #2407](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2407).

The plugin probes the runtime capability
(`ctx.agentLoop.supportsAssistantPrefill`). On a patched host the ceiling text is
an assistant tail and no system-prompt section is added. On a stock host it
keeps the same text and trigger as a system-prompt section (see the fallback
table below); that is survivability, not the complete opencode surface.

| Surface | opencode / patched harness | This plugin on a stock 0.2.1 host |
|---|---|---|
| Role of `MAX_STEPS_PROMPT` | Assistant-role continuation at the end of the request | System-prompt section for that step |
| Session transcript / stats / compaction | Request-only (header), not a session message | Also not a session message (system section is reassembled) |
| How strictly models stop / wrap up | Tuned for an assistant tail | May treat a system reminder more weakly or more strongly |
| Token placement | Extra assistant tokens on that request | Extra system tokens on that request |
| Reconstructable requests | Logged on `request/header` | Rebuilt from the live prompt assembly |

The fallback is selected at runtime; the patch is not dropped when a host can
run without it.

Provider-visible `format`/`toolChoice` remains an unpatched proposal; omo's
regular path does not use it.

Everything else runs on unmodified dsh seams: the preset is declared by the
official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row, the role picker occupies the
existing `conversation.input.left` slot, and role settings use the official
settings form Remote.

Runners and reproduction notes live in [`tests/benches/`](tests/benches/README.md); reports are written to `docs/exps/`. The scientific methodology (paired design, McNemar/bootstrap/TOST, A/A noise floor, trace alignment, cache and latency protocols) is documented in [`docs/exps/2026-08-16-scientific-bench-methodology.md`](docs/exps/2026-08-16-scientific-bench-methodology.md). Design highlights:

- Run an isolated-port dsh (`opencode-omo` mode, isolated `$DSH_HOME`) and the machine's installed opencode + oh-my-openagent (isolated `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`).
- Both use `deepseek-official/deepseek-v4-pro` (dpsk v4 pro); the API key comes from the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` environment variable. Scripts hardcode no machine paths or secrets.
- Tiered benches: L1 HumanEval, L2 MBPP, L3 SWE-bench-verified-mini (sampled), comparing pass@1, CoT/reasoning exposure, tool-call chains (read/edit/write/bash/test/subagents), and final patches/answers.
- Performance: `bench_metrics.mjs` normalizes token usage (including `cacheRead`) and tool timestamps on both sides; `eval_perf.mjs` / `eval_swe_perf.mjs` produce cache hit rate, TTFT, step duration, and per-tool timing offline (see report §5).
- **MBPP fix**: MBPP rows have no `entry_point`; the scripts infer the function name from the first `assert fn(...)` or the reference `def fn`. The old implementation hardcoded `Function name: undefined`, which was the root cause of MBPP behavioral divergence (see report §0 and §6.4).
- Raw bench data is downloaded to `tests/benches/.data/` and is **not versioned**; `fetch-benches.sh` reproduces the downloads and `s

| Upstream | Version | Commit | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
